speaker: Unknown
quote_text: Good evening everyone. Reminder, no photos or videos on match day. Thank you very much. Welcome to this post-match press conference. Please ensure you've got a microphone in your hand before you ask a question, and please ensure that all mobile phones are either on mute or vibrate just so that we don't have any disruptions, please. Thank you very much. Yeah. Do you think that electing to field first which on a wicket which looked very good for batting >> [clears throat] >> was a mistake or was it influenced by many other factors? Um I guess you can look in hindsight, um but I think you know, it was a pretty good wicket throughout. Um there wasn't much for I guess the bowlers know, the cutters weren't really holding, not much spin. So, I think either way you look at it, I think, um you know, if we could have got a couple in the power play, you know, squeeze them a little bit through the middle, 220 could have been, you know, chased down on a on a very good wicket. So, um but I think, you know, credit to Sanju and Abhishek at the top, you know, to get 90, I think, off the power play. It's pretty tough from there. Mitch, um what was the plan in the power play because it seemed like your focus was going wide and hitting the ball out of the hitters' reach. What was the plan that you guys fixed for the power play because you mentioned playing against India the power not losing the power play was really huge in the pre-match. Yeah, I think, um you know, there wasn't a lot of, I guess, seam or swing to start. So, I think it's, you know, the bowlers trying to do what they can to get out of the hitting arc. Um you know, we know how good both Sanju, Abhishek, Kishan are are are hitting, you know, all over the wicket. So, um yeah, I think the you know, whichever way you look at it, there's no perfect plan when guys are going. You know, I think, you know, it is it is hard to stop when guys are going like that. So, whether it was a few more yorkers or uh you know, closing out balls, I think we tried the wide stuff and and then, you know, we tried the two on the leg side. So, we tried everything. Um but yeah, I think credit has to go to the way they set that power play up and then from there you can you can go pretty hard and and and to get a good score like they did. Uh Mitch, second over of the inning, Glenn Philip bowled a decent over and gave only five runs. Why he was not given the ball again? Um yeah, I think the way, you know, they played the over, Abhishek I thought played that very smart. I know at times he he comes a little bit hard at the off spinner, but he you know, he gave it over to Sandhu and then I think, you know, the first kind of three overs is when the ball is doing its most and then I think you can really, you know, capitalize on the last three of the power play like like they did. So, it was always going to be hard. I think if Sandhu got out, definitely would have been another option for GP to bowl to the two left-handers, but um yeah, when you're not taking wickets, it's always it's always a challenge. Mitch, uh hard luck. Um you have just said it was like you tried everything out there. You've played a lot of T20 cricket. How good a team do you think you've just lost the final to? Yeah, a very good team. Um you know, I think they they know how to play in these conditions. They play on a lot of flat wickets um against against quality sides and they showed that again today that once they're going, it's it's pretty tough to stop. So, I think for us it was, you know, whether it was being braver with yorkers or bouncers. Um I think we tried a lot of the cutters into the wicket that, you know, on wickets that aren't offering a much, you know, they just kind of go as well. So, I think you know, they did knock it around at times. And I think when we did, you know, use the slower bounces, the yorkers for that little phase in the middle we're able to slow them down, but I think again, the damage was done. And then, you know, Dube come in at the end and hitting, you know, they're all striking it pretty well at the moment. So, I think, yeah, you know, 230 we could have taken 230 on a on a pretty good wicket. Yeah. Mitch, uh hi. Uh just wanted to know about the selection of the 11. Throughout this tournament we have seen that some of most of the teams attack India with spin and they have struggled against spinners. You have uh of the option of playing Cole, but you decided to go ahead with uh Jacob. So, can you please talk about this particular selection? Yeah, it was a tough one. I mean, we saw at Kolkata I think the match up again was, you know, off spin to their top three. Um you know, I made a bet the wicket, the mix soil, you know, usually has no spin. No, it has always a little bit of bounce and I think bowling my overs, Xavier's and and Chakravarthy's, there was no real spin at any stage. Um so, I think, you know, which way you go, I think you know, there was potentially a bit of bounce for the seamers, but I think at the end of the day it's it's an execution whoever is bowling. Um you know, I think when you bowl, you know, nice areas for a period of time you could, you know, get an out of overs. I think that was the main thing, you know, it was wasn't trying to get wickets at times. It was, you know, how you be defensive defensive to be attacking. Um and I think when we did that well, we, you know, we managed to squeeze I think a period of four overs and we they lost four wickets, but you know, outside of that it was it was it was a few runs. Um Mitch, um you've been part of a pretty uh you've been part of a few finals losses, especially after you've screamed through a semi-final. Um you must be getting pretty sick of the feeling. Yeah, I guess it's not ideal losing losing series in finals, but you know, like I said the other day, you know, you get to the situation you're coming up against teams that are also playing very good cricket. Um you know, India in a final in India is always going to be a challenge. We knew that. Definitely underdogs going into the game and um they they showed their class again tonight. Um you know, with their batting performance and then you know, everything kind of has to go well when you chasing 250 and you know, losing wickets in the power play is um it's always a challenge. I think that was the tail of the the day was at two power plays. I think we were three for 40 odd and they were 90 odd for none. Hi Mitch. Uh you played against India in the bilaterals where Sanju was a total disaster just over 45 runs or 46 and here he was scored about 90 runs. So, what did you think make up him? What amendments he made to his batting or where did he go right and where did he go wrong earlier? Yeah, I guess it's unfortunate for us that he he was saving all those runs for the World Cup. Um I think you know, in a few of those games he was look like he was trying to hit from ball one or you know, and then I think tonight even the other night he gave himself a chance, gave himself a few balls and then you know, I think on these wickets when you're in you can really cash in and I think Abhishek was at the same. He padded back a little bit of spin at the start and then you know, they seem once they once they're both ready and faced a few balls they were they were ready to go and and they did go. So, I think you know, I think that was the play for us was trying to see if we could bowl full and get you know, early poles but um we obviously didn't tonight. Hi Mitch. Um so, you just uh you've said that your bowlers could have been braver with their uh yorkers and and bounces and obviously the uh your batting innings chasing a massive total with didn't go fantastically. Have you let yourselves down to tonight and if so, why do you think? Yeah, I think so. I mean, you know, you you always have um when you come up against a very good team in a final, you always you know, want to do well and I think we obviously we all know that we weren't at our best tonight and if you aren't at your best against a very good team, you're going to be exposed and um that's kind of what we were tonight. So, um I think, you know, we probably look at some options with the ball and and with the bat. Um you know, we can reflect on that again. You know, you know you have to be going pretty well against India in a final. Um I think, you know, some of the options with the ball at the start, you know, we could have potentially done things a little bit different, but I think when two guys are going in the power play, um as we saw I guess our winnings against South Africa as well, it's it's pretty tough to stop guys when they're going. Um so, what whatever that looks like, we'll reflect on that, you know, going forward. Coming up against, you know, teams on very flat wickets, um what does it look like? It might be a little bit different and then I guess with the bat, you know, I guess you you're not going to win a chase in the power play, but you're going to lose one. Um but I guess here 250 tonight was always going to be a a tough score. Uh Mitch, uh before before the final, you put out a sweet little note on Twitter, even apologizing to your people back home for playing on a Sunday and also asking them to wake up early in the morning to support you and watch the final. Having come some having come so close and you know, being a finishing as yet another finalist, what message do you have for your people back home? Yeah, I guess it's, you know, I guess that's thanks to the the fans back home for following us. Um yeah, might have to go to work obviously without a without a trophy today. Um but, you know, we get obviously great support back home um and we get great support here as well. You know, and it was, you know, it was awesome to to play in front of so many people tonight. Um obviously had a few blue shirts on, not many black shirts, but, you know, again it's it's always a great occasion and it's always cool for us to play in front of, you know, so many people. So, um yeah, it was obviously wasn't our greatest effort tonight. Um came up against a very good team. Um so, yeah. I can thank just thanking the fans back home. Hi Mitch. >> [clears throat] >> Hard luck today, but uh just as we're talking about looking forward and what do you say to your fans? A bit of a spin-off on that question. You don't have to wait that much for the next World Cup to come up these days. I mean, you've got one next year in South Africa and then the then the T20 one is in Australia. So, you don't have to play in subcontinent conditions, maybe in conditions we do enjoy or have a comfort zone. So, uh any chances or any thoughts on that as you as you look ahead to end this uh drought in the sequence? Um yeah, it's probably quite far away there. Um I think yeah, we'll reflect as a group um tonight, you know, over the next few days uh of I guess this tournament and what it looked like. I think, you know, to make it to a final is obviously a pretty good effort from the boys and, you know, they should be very proud of their efforts throughout this tournament. Um yeah, and then I guess the next kind of major event is one-days in South Africa. Like you said, it's going to play slightly different to to what we expect here and then um our next T20 World Cup is in Australia and New Zealand. So, um it'll be nice if get a few a few fans in the the crowd there and um and I guess familiar conditions. And I think that's, you know, one of the hardest things is to to win a World Cup in your country. Um so, for India to do that, you know, this you know, this obviously comes with a lot of added pressure, you know, home fans. Um so, for them to, you know, win this trophy tonight is, you know, they should be very proud of that. I made stuff luck. You speak about how difficult it is to win a World Cup at home. How could you sum up how intimidating it is to play a World Cup final in India. Um Some some of the mental challenge that undertakes and we always talk about chasing in a final. How difficult have did you find that out to be today especially when all the chatter has been about India's batting and the kind of template they set in the semi-final and how it seems to have replicated itself. Yeah, I think and first on the playing in India is always a a great occasion. Um you know, I've been coming here for a few years now and you know, every time you play in front of that many people it's it's very exciting. It always comes with you know, the challenges especially being captain trying to get hold of your fielders and and stuff when you can't hear anyone. Um but you know, again it's you know, that's what we play the game for is to play in front of you know, people that are huge fans of cricket. Um so I think you know, there was definitely Yeah, obviously finals come with nerves and pressures but I think you know, there was definitely a lot of pressure on on India as well um to perform in front of you know, so many people when they they did that outstandingly well today. Um So I think credit to them and um I think Yeah, I think you know, I guess you look at our semi-final if you can take wickets in the power play, squeeze through the middle and then you know, restrict a team to you know, even 200 um on a very good wicket that could have been chasable. I think 250 you know, you need a lot of things to go your way. Um so and I think that's you know, you got to give credit to India for that the way they came out and played and knew that they needed a good score and you know, I think you can bet on yourself, you know, bet us out of the game I guess with the score of 250. Thank you.
title: Mitchell Santner post-match press conference - India vs New Zealand Final
